title: Performance evaluation of heat recovery steam generators in a combined cycle power plant using pinch analysis: A case study from Sudan
content:
Abstract

This study investigates the performance of Heat Recovery Steam Generators (HRSGs) in a combined cycle power plant in Sudan, focusing on the comparative analysis of two fuel types: Light Diesel Oil (LDO) and Heavy Cycle Gas Oil (HCGO). Using Pinch Analysis, a method for optimizing thermal energy recovery, the research assesses heat exchange efficiency within HRSG units operating under different fuel scenarios. Thermodynamic properties, including supply and target temperatures, heat capacity, and heat load, were analyzed using MATLAB modeling. The outcomes show lower unutilized thermal energy for the LDO operating scenario that was looked at (22,053 MJ/h) compared with the HCGO case (29,108 MJ/h). On site, plant observations also pointed at dissimilar deposit development between the two modes of operation, but those remarks were rather qualitative and they were not taken as measured proof for fouling performance. Operational data and fuel quality records from 2015 to 2017 further support LDO's advantages in terms of system reliability and maintenance. Overall, the findings demonstrate that LDO is the more efficient and reliable fuel for HRSG-based systems, with Pinch Analysis proving to be an effective tool for guiding fuel selection and enhancing energy utilization in thermal power plants.
